description: Human GLP-1R 6X18 chain R, same belt construct and coordinates as hGLP1R_6X18_belt (184 residues, segments 136-161/181-246/267-321/360-396, membrane-facing hydrophobics charge-swapped). Retargeted from the extracellular cap to the TMD orthosteric pore for a cyclic peptide. Depth measured along the TM-bundle axis with 0 A at the ledge plane: the mouth/vestibule (0 to -6 A) has 7.2-7.7 A free radius, the constriction (-8 to -12 A) 3.7-3.9 A, -14 to -18 A 2.8-3.3 A, and the deep channel (-20 to -26 A) only 1.3-2.2 A, ~530 A^3 total. Native GLP-1(7-14) in the same frame spans only -17.2 (His7) to -7.3 A (Ser14), so residues below -18 A are channel WALL contacted by peptide side chains from above, not volume a macrocycle can occupy. Hard hotspots (gated at min_hotspot_contact_final 0.66, so 2 of 3 required): Gln234 (-13.7), Trp306 (-13.4) and Arg310 (-16.2), the deepest lumen-facing residues a ring can reach - all three contact native His7. Soft hotspots steer deeper without gating: Arg190 (-20.7), Glu387 (-20.8) and Tyr152 (-18.8), each contacted by native Glu9/Ala8 from above, so reachable by a side chain without descending. Coldspots are the 70-residue membrane belt and peripheral shell carried over unchanged from the belt target. The ledge and extracellular mouth (136-139, 198, 204, 210, 211, 213, 221, 292, 295, 301, 302) are deliberately left FREE, not coldspotted: the ring is meant to protrude through the mouth. The belt campaign's top soft hotspots Trp214/Glu294/Arg376 are removed - no hotspot sits on the top.
